id_kind: local request identifier, not platform call ID
result: one essential missing explanation requires repair

findings.issue: The inverse correspondence from the exponential-component ratio to a causal kernel is asserted without teaching transform theory or an equivalent direct impulse-response derivation.
findings.repair: Use the post-impulse homogeneous equation and zero-position/unit-velocity-jump conditions to determine the double-exponential coefficient; preserve normalization and numerical example.

coverage_judgments.reason: intentional-consolidation | Chapter opening and `sec:EYE-LIMITS`: abstract's upstream finding and specific integrator proposal are separated. Author affiliations omitted as nonteaching.

covered | `sec:EYE-PATHWAY`, `sec:EYE-RECORDINGS`, `sec:EYE-FORWARD-FIT`, `sec:EYE-INVERSE-FILTER`: fixation, prior recordings, small rate effects, inverse prediction and mean correlation. Broad debate about drift's visual function omitted because this chapter teaches mechanism and inference.
covered | `sec:EYE-SHARED-VARIANCE`, `sec:EYE-FIGURES`: Fig. 1, R-squared explanatory fraction, independence bound and common-input interpretation.
covered | `sec:EYE-INVERSE-FILTER`, `sec:EYE-CHI`, `sec:EYE-FIGURES`: Fig. 2 kernel constants, displacement correlation, 302 segments, chi and estimation error axes.
covered | `sec:EYE-CHI`, `sec:EYE-FILTERED-MSD`, `sec:EYE-PATHWAY`: gain transfer, common variance result, observed time dependence, and rationale for integrator.
covered | `sec:EYE-MEASUREMENT-NOISE`, `sec:EYE-FILTERED-MSD`, `sec:EYE-SCALING`, `sec:EYE-FIGURES`: Fig. 3, Eq. 1 with normalization caveat, amplitude versus shape constraints.

covered | `sec:EYE-CIRCUIT-MODEL`, `sec:EYE-SHARED-VARIANCE`, `sec:EYE-LIMITS`, `sec:EYE-FIGURES`: feedback's role, intrinsic independence basis, Fig. 4 neutral-direction diffusion and simulation validation logic.
covered | `sec:EYE-CIRCUIT-MODEL`, `sec:EYE-FIGURES`: Fig. 5 stages, smoother physical output, MSD match, simulated analysis controls.
Recording/fitting methods are taught, but the central inversion still asserts an unexplained inverse-transform correspondence.

covered | `sec:EYE-CHI`, `sec:EYE-MEASUREMENT-NOISE`, `sec:EYE-FILTERED-MSD`: Eq. 8 displacement correlation, Eq. 11–17 covariance assumptions and weighting, Eq. 18–22 noise/MSD derivation. Eq. 9 finite-sample covariance-error calculation is described by its role and recorded as the paper's method, not rederived; Eq. 10 rate of uncertainty for R is not used in a new guide result.

covered | `sec:EYE-CIRCUIT-MODEL`, `sec:EYE-SCALING`: Eqs. 23–31 and 34 roles, units and steady state; heterogeneous tuning, threshold and nonoscillation constraints; CV and spike thinning. Exact empirical slope-distribution coefficients of Eqs. 27, 32–33 and empirical CV fit coefficients in Eq. 35 intentionally omitted, since no population simulation is being reproduced.

intentional-consolidation | `sec:EYE-RECORDINGS` covers active-cell/trial exclusions and `sec:EYE-CHI` error interpretation. Data/code availability recorded under source access above. Bibliography consolidated into the guide reference workflow, without copying every cited work.
intentional-omission | Remaining bibliography, acknowledgments, disclosures, license and correspondence add no teaching step. Main source citation and access evidence retained.
intentional-consolidation | Inventory used to ensure all ten Extended Data figures and notes were accounted for; guide explanation locations below. SI parameter files are recorded as not downloaded.
covered | `sec:EYE-SHARED-VARIANCE`: Eqs. S1–S2 expanded into residual-variance proof. `sec:EYE-SCALING` introduces the question of drift's contribution to measured CV.
covered | `sec:EYE-SCALING`: Eqs. S3–S6, covariance integral for within-segment Brownian variance, reciprocal-rate expansion, numerical CV and unit conversion.
covered | `sec:EYE-CIRCUIT-MODEL`, `sec:EYE-FIGURES`: distinguish internal spike noise driving diffusion from direct output noise, and explain feedback motivation and role.

intentional-consolidation | `sec:EYE-CIRCUIT-MODEL`, footnote p2-feedback: feedback effects combined with final main Eq. 34 and Extended Data Fig. 3. Stale supplement cross references and 15K parameter statement disclosed; final main 30,000 count used. Bibliography consolidated.
intentional-omission | Supplemental reference continuation; no separate derivation or result. Sources cited through paper/SI locations and coordinator reference list.

covered | `sec:EYE-CHI`, `sec:EYE-FIGURES`: Extended Data Fig. 1, uncertainty and estimates outside the underlying fraction range. Caption's repeated monkey label treated as a source typo, not used for a new claim.
covered | `sec:EYE-MEASUREMENT-NOISE`, `sec:EYE-FIGURES`: Extended Data Fig. 2, fixed-coil control, twice-position-variance offset and simulated recovery check.

covered | `sec:EYE-CIRCUIT-MODEL`, `sec:EYE-FIGURES`: Extended Data Fig. 3, feedback/no-feedback fit and lag-dependent slope changes. Individual alternate simulation counts intentionally not repeated.

covered | `sec:EYE-FIGURES`: Extended Data Fig. 4, no-central-drive control and negative noisy chi estimate; Extended Data Fig. 5, second monkey parameter adjustments and nonunique fit. Exact alternate CV regression coefficients omitted with no reproduction.
covered | `sec:EYE-PATHWAY`, `sec:EYE-FIGURES`: Extended Data Fig. 6, motor/internuclear classification by response parameters. No new claim about perfect cell-type certainty.

covered | `sec:EYE-RECORDINGS`, `sec:EYE-FIGURES`: Extended Data Figs. 7–8, segment lengths/counts and rank-correlation confirmation. Histogram bins and separate rank-test p-value omitted because neither changes the taught inference.
covered | `sec:EYE-CIRCUIT-MODEL`, `sec:EYE-FIGURES`: Extended Data Fig. 9, diverse tuning and motor-response parameters.

covered | `sec:EYE-FIGURES`: Extended Data Fig. 10, output spike noise removal preserves internal spike noise and has little effect beyond 50 ms. The finest simulated lag effects are consolidated because the experiment's measurement noise limits that range.
